rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Human activity pushes five imbalances past nature's feedback limits. The enhanced greenhouse effect — CO₂, CH₄, N₂O and CFCs trapping outgoing heat — drives warming, melting Himalayan glaciers, rising seas and erratic monsoons. CFCs shred stratospheric ozone, Earth's UV sunscreen, inviting skin cancer and plankton loss until the Montreal Protocol acted.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Greenhouse warming ≈ +15 °C − (−18 °C) = about 33 °C.
Acid rain: SO2 and NOx → sulphuric and nitric acids, pH below about 5.6.
Ozone hole: column below about 220 DU, against a normal column of about 300 DU.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Ozone hole vs global warming:** ozone depletion = CFCs destroying stratospheric O₃ → more UV; global warming = greenhouse gases trapping heat → higher temperature. Different problems, different treaties (Montreal vs Paris).  ·  **Eutrophication vs pollution generally:** eutrophication is specifically nutrient over-enrichment — not any contamination.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Do not blame the ozone hole for glacier melt. That is the greenhouse side.  ·  Spell Mikania micrantha and Eichhornia crassipes once. After that the common name is enough.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Water hyacinth (Eichhornia)*** — invasive weed clogging Nepali lakes and canals.  ·  ***Mikania micrantha (banmara)*** — "mile-a-minute" vine smothering Chitwan's vegetation.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: The 2024 eutrophication question (3m) demands cause + effect chain — write it as a numbered sequence.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Write four labelled paragraphs, one imbalance each.  ·  Compute the 33 °C greenhouse difference from −18 °C and +15 °C.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "Bloom → Shade → Die → Decompose → Suffocate" — five words, full marks.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Short answer (2m):** Why is the natural greenhouse effect beneficial? **Answer.** Without any greenhouse gases the Earth's average surface temperature would be about **−18 °C**; the natural effect (CO₂, CH₄, water vapour) keeps it near **+15 °C**, making liquid water and life possible.…

rows.text: Most-tested: eutrophication (2024). Diagram-worthy: eutrophication sequence diagram; ozone chemistry cartoon.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **The eutrophication causal chain** is the exam's favourite sequence — memorise: nutrients → bloom → shade → death → decomposition → oxygen crash → fish kill.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Greenhouse gases: CO₂, CH₄, N₂O, CFCs, water vapour → enhanced greenhouse effect → warming, sea-level rise, erratic monsoons; mitigation: renewables, afforestation, Paris Agreement.  ·  Ozone: stratospheric O₃ absorbs UV-B; CFCs destroy it (1 Cl → ~100,000 O₃); Montreal Protocol 1987; effects: skin cancer, cataracts, phytoplankton loss.  ·  Acid rain: SO₂ + NOₓ → H₂SO₄/HNO₃ (pH<5.6); kills forests, lakes, monuments.  ·  Invasion: water hyacinth, Mikania (banmara), lantana; enemy-release; control by quarantine and biocontrol.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The Montreal Protocol (1987) is the only environmental treaty ratified by every UN member state.

rows.text: Eutrophication: N/P runoff → algal bloom → light blockage → decomposition → O₂ depletion → fish death.  ·  "Every imbalance is a cycle pushed past its feedback limits."  ·  Why is the Montreal Protocol considered more successful than climate treaties? **Answer.** Because its problem was chemically narrow and its solution was cheap: only a **single family of chemicals (CFCs/halons)**, made by a few companies, with ready substitutes and a measurable atmospheric target.…
